title.zh: 卷一百二十七 載記第二十七 慕容德

proposal.before: They ran decoy coffers out each gate and hid his true burial in the hills.
proposal.after: That night they prepared more than ten coffins and sent them out through the four gates, burying him secretly in the mountain valleys; in the end, no one knew where his body lay.
proposal.reason: 棺 means coffins, not coffers; preserve the number, nocturnal setting and uncertain location. The text does not explicitly identify any particular coffin as a decoy.

context.zh: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。
context.idiomatic: He named Murong Chao crown prince and issued a broad amnesty.
context.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict making Chao crown prince, amnestied the realm, and for sons continuing fathers raised each man's rank two grades.

context.zh: 其月死，即義熙元年也，時年七十。
context.idiomatic: He died the same month, in the first year of Yixi, at seventy sui.
context.literal: That month he died; it was the first year of Yixi, and at the time his age was seventy sui.

context.zh: 乃夜為十餘棺，分出四門，潛葬山谷，竟不知其屍之所在。
context.idiomatic: They ran decoy coffers out each gate and hid his true burial in the hills.
context.literal: That night they made more than ten coffins, sent them out the four gates separately, and secretly buried him in mountain valleys; in the end none knew where his corpse lay.
He held the throne five years.

context.idiomatic: His temple posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu.
context.literal: He was posthumously titled Emperor Xianwu.

proposal.before: He was posthumously titled Emperor Xianwu.
proposal.after: He was given the posthumous title Emperor Xianwu, which the Jin historian regarded as illegitimate.
proposal.reason: 偽諡 marks a posthumous title as illegitimate from the historiographer’s perspective; this formulation needs independent contextual and stylistic review.
